sections.content: Pre-Columbian societies had different forms of authority and social organisation. The passive voice (era recibido por, eran administradas por) is common for describing power relations from the point of view of who received or was subject to them.

items.spanish: El tributo era recibido por el gobernante, aunque las comunidades conservaban ciertas formas de autonomía.
items.english: Tribute was received by the ruler, although communities kept certain forms of autonomy.

items.spanish: Las tierras eran administradas por autoridades locales que respondían a un poder central.
items.english: The land was administered by local authorities who answered to a central power.

items.spanish: El poder político no era ejercido de la misma manera en todas las sociedades.
items.english: Political power was not exercised the same way in every society.

items.spanish: La jerarquía organizaba las posiciones sociales.

sections.content: Ser + participio (era recibido, eran administradas) foregrounds the thing affected rather than the person doing the action — a step up from the active-voice sentences Core's earlier units use.
